speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing hand tremors and recent memory issues; to understand the cause, I must ask you a few questions. First, did these symptoms start suddenly or did they develop gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the progressive nature of the tremor starting in one hand and now affecting fine motor skills like reading is concerning. Your wife's observation of memory decline, particularly with finances, suggests cognitive involvement. Has he noticed any changes in his personality, such as increased apathy, or difficulty with planning and organizing tasks?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of a resting tremor, soft speech, reduced facial expressions, and memory decline is highly suggestive of Parkinson's disease with dementia. To confirm this and assess the severity of the cognitive impairment, have you noticed any changes in his ability to recognize familiar people or places?
